statement: AMD claims the MI455X delivers 10 to 15% more tokens per second per GPU and up to 30% more tokens per dollar than NVIDIA's Vera Rubin generation.
why: If the cost-per-token gap holds in real deployments, buyers gain a pricing lever against the incumbent for the first time in this generation.

impact.mechanism: A cheaper cost per token from a second supplier increases effective compute supply per dollar and pressures incumbent pricing.

evidence.excerpt: AMD claims '10 to 15% more tokens per second per GPU' and 'up to 30% more tokens per dollar'

confidence.basis: Vendor performance claim relayed by one secondary outlet with no independent benchmark; recorded qualitatively with no value.
